messages:
elaine: dropping a couple quick direction mocks for the very-first-run flow. thinking: a condensed "cue" rail that sits left of the canvas and can expand into the full setup checklist. want a quick sanity pass on UX, a11y, and any implementation flags.

sam: love the idea. does the rail persist after completion or collapse into a lightweight status chip?

marta: metric-wise we see higher click-through when the surface remains visible but not intrusive. recommend persistent but dismissible. include 'remind me later' to reduce friction.

oliver: accessibility: current contrast on the CTA chip (#5a9bd6 on white) is ~3.8:1 at 14px. needs to hit 4.5:1. also the visual focus ring is faint on dark mode.

tariq: engineering constraints: if the rail is sticky it must account for the console header height, otherwise it overlaps on small viewports. i'll prototype using position: sticky with top equal to header. animation should avoid layout thrash.

sam: microcopy proposal: swap "Start with a sample project" -> "Try a sample project"; "Finish setup" -> "Complete setup". shorter verbs feel friendlier. also suggest clarifying the skip action: "Skip for now" vs "Remind me later" (different telemetry semantics).

marta: good call on telemetry. we should have separate events for skip vs snooze. i'll add keys.

elaine: oliver 14 can you list the a11y must-fix items? tariq 14 can you prototype sticky + reduced-motion? sam 14 update frames with contrast and microcopy variants? marta 14 draft the experiment matrix?

oliver: checklist: 1) raise CTA contrast to >=4.5:1 or increase text size to 16px; 2) ensure keyboard focus is always visible (4px ring, high-contrast); 3) when the rail expands move focus to the first actionable control and set aria-expanded on the toggle; 4) provide a "Skip to main content" focusable link; 5) avoid aria-live for non-critical updates.

tariq: for the expand/collapse animation i'm planning this minimal approach to keep compositing-only and respect prefers-reduced-motion:

```css
.cue-rail { position: sticky; top: 72px; will-change: transform, opacity; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1), opacity 120ms linear; }
.cue-rail--collapsed { transform: translateY(-6px); opacity: 0.97; }
.cue-rail--expanded { transform: translateY(0); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .cue-rail { transition: none; } }
```

sam: looks reasonable. keep the motion distance tiny so screen readers don't misinterpret. also ensure the expanded checklist uses a logical heading order.

marta: experiment matrix draft: control (banner) | variant A (persistent rail + control copy) | variant B (persistent rail + new microcopy) — primary metric: first-run completion rate; secondary: time-to-first-api-call; guardrail: increased support ticket mentions. i'll post the matrix in tracking doc.

elaine: deploy-bot reminder 14 design freeze for onboarding surfaces this Fri 5pm PT.

deploy-bot: reminder acknowledged. please link final comps to the release ticket.

sam: i'll update Figma frames by Thu EOD and tag oliver for a11y sign-off.

oliver: quick accessibility follow-up: ensure that keyboard users can close the rail and that the close control is reachable by tab order before other interactive items. also include aria-labels on icons.

tariq: implementation Q 14 should the rail be included in the DOM always, or rendered conditionally? for keyboard focus it's easier to keep it in DOM and hide visually. opinions?

marta: keep in DOM but aria-hidden when collapsed to avoid screen reader noise. we'll check analytics to ensure that hidden-but-present doesn't inflate impressions.

elaine: action items summary: sam - update comps (contrast + copy + header/hierarchy); tariq - prototype sticky offset + reduced-motion and conditional-render guidance; oliver - final a11y checklist sign-off; marta - experiment matrix + telemetry keys. scheduling a 20m sync Wed 10am to review.

sam: noted, thanks team. :thumbsup:

elaine: thanks all 14 closing out unless any late blockers show up.
